items.prompt: Black has just moved. Anything to worry about? Show the threat by moving a Black piece, or say there is none.

claims.statement: The pawn on e5 attacks the bishop.
The knight on f3 guards the bishop.
If White passes, the pawn wins the bishop for a pawn.

hints: Which of your pieces does a black pawn attack? Pawns capture one square diagonally forward.
The bishop is guarded. Does that make the attack harmless? Count the points after the recapture.
The pawn takes the bishop, the knight takes the pawn: Black gives 1 point and wins 3.
items.explain: The pawn on e5 attacks the bishop. The knight guards it, but if the pawn takes and the knight takes back, Black has swapped a pawn for a bishop. As a rule of thumb, a cheaper piece attacking a dearer one is a threat even when the target is guarded.

items.prompt: Black has just moved. Anything to worry about? Show the threat by moving a Black piece, or say there is none.

claims.statement: No white piece is loose.
The bishop guards the pawn on b2.
If White passed, Black could not win anything by force.

hints: Which white piece does the queen attack?
Is that piece guarded? Imagine the queen takes it.
If the queen takes the b-pawn, the bishop takes the queen.
items.explain: The queen attacks the b2 pawn, but the bishop guards it. If the queen took, the bishop would take the queen: 9 points for 1. Nothing is threatened, so White may follow a plan of its own.

feedback_by_move.b5b2: Taking on b2 would lose the queen to the bishop. The pawn is guarded, so this is not a real threat.

items.prompt: Black has just moved. Anything to worry about? Show the threat by moving a Black piece, or say there is none.

claims.statement: If White passes, the queen takes on h2 with checkmate.
Only the king guards h2.

hints: Look at the squares near the white king. What does the queen aim at?
The bishop stands behind the queen on the same diagonal. What does that do to a capture on h2?
The queen takes h2 and the bishop guards it, so the king cannot take back. The rook blocks f1.
items.explain: The queen and bishop line up on the diagonal towards h2. Only the king guards that pawn, and the queen on h2 would be guarded by the bishop, while the rook on f1 blocks the king's other square. That is checkmate.

items.prompt: Black has just moved. Anything to worry about? Show the threat by moving a Black piece, or say there is none.

claims.statement: No white piece is loose.
A pawn guards the bishop on e3.
A pawn guards the bishop on c3.
If White passed, Black could not win anything by force.

hints: The knight attacks two bishops. Is either of them loose?
Look at the pawns next to each bishop.
If the knight takes either bishop, a pawn takes the knight: an even swap, so no one gains.
items.explain: The knight attacks both bishops, but a pawn guards each. Taking either one only swaps a knight for a bishop. A fork only wins something when you can win one of the pieces.

feedback_by_move.d5e3: After the knight takes on e3, the f-pawn takes back: a knight for a bishop. Even swap, no gain.
feedback_by_move.d5c3: After the knight takes on c3, the b-pawn takes back: a knight for a bishop. Even swap, no gain.

items.prompt: Black has just moved. Anything to worry about? Show the threat by moving a Black piece, or say there is none.

claims.statement: The knight on e3 is attacked and nothing guards it.
If White passes, the rook wins the knight.

hints: The knight's move itself attacks nothing. What did it uncover?
Which black piece now looks down an open file?
The rook on e8 attacks the knight on e3, and nothing guards it.
items.explain: The black knight stepped off the e-file. That uncovered the rook, which now looks down the open file at a white knight that nothing guards.

items.prompt: Black's bishop stands on b6 and White's knight on d4. Black has just moved. What does Black threaten? Move a Black piece to show it.

claims.statement: The knight on d4 is attacked and nothing guards it.
If White passes, the bishop wins the knight.

hints: Follow the bishop's diagonal.
Does anything guard the knight?
The bishop takes the knight and nothing takes back.
items.explain: The bishop attacks the knight along the diagonal and nothing guards the knight, so Black threatens to win it.

items.prompt: The same position, but a white pawn now stands on e3. Black has just moved. Anything to worry about? Show the threat or say there is none.

claims.statement: No white piece is loose.
The pawn on e3 guards the knight.
If White passes, the capture gains Black nothing.

hints: The bishop still attacks the knight. What changed?
Count the swap if the bishop takes.
The bishop takes the knight and the pawn takes the bishop: 3 for 3.
items.explain: The pawn on e3 guards the knight. If the bishop takes, the pawn takes back, and the swap is even. The threat has gone.

feedback_by_move.b6d4: After the bishop takes, the pawn takes back: a bishop for a knight. Even swap, so it is not a real threat.

items.prompt: The same position, but White's h-pawn has stepped from h2 to h3. Black has just moved. What does Black threaten? Move a Black piece to show it.

claims.statement: The knight on d4 is still attacked and nothing guards it.
If White passes, the bishop still wins the knight.

hints: Compare it with the first position. What is different, and does it touch the knight or the bishop?
A pawn move on the other wing changes neither the attack nor the guard.
The bishop still takes a knight that nothing guards.
items.explain: The h-pawn has nothing to do with the knight or the bishop, so the threat is exactly as before. Not every change matters: ask whether it touches the target, the attacker or the line between them.

items.prompt: White has just captured on e5 with a knight. What does White threaten? Move a White piece to show the strongest threat you can find (a second, smaller threat is also accepted).

claims.statement: If Black makes no useful move, White has a forced mate in two starting with Bxf7+.
Black could take the queen.
If Black takes the queen with Bxd1, then Bxf7+ Ke7 Nd5 is checkmate.
Black's best reply is dxe5, which removes the mating knight.
A smaller threat: the bishop on g4 is attacked by the knight and the queen and nothing guards it.

hints: Look at the bishop on c4 and the f7 pawn. Who guards f7?
A bishop capture on f7 gives check. Where can the king go?
The king can only go to e7, and a knight move then gives checkmate.
items.explain: Bxf7+ is the big threat: the king has one square, and a knight then gives checkmate. If Black takes the queen, the mate follows. Black's best reply is dxe5, which removes the mating knight. Nxg4 also attacks a loose bishop, so it is accepted, but the mate is the bigger threat.

feedback_by_move.e5g4: Accepted: the bishop on g4 is loose, so that is a real second threat. Look again for a bigger one, with check, on f7.

items.prompt: Black's rook is on the open e-file and Black has just moved. What does Black threaten? Move a Black piece to show it.

claims.statement: If White passes, ...Re1 is checkmate.
No white piece covers e1.

hints: Follow the open file to the first rank.
Can the king step anywhere after a check on e1?
Three pawns shut the king in.
items.explain: The rook reaches e1 with check, nothing covers e1 and the pawns box the king in, so Black threatens checkmate.

items.prompt: The same position, but the white h-pawn stands on h3. Black has just moved. Anything to worry about? Show the threat or say there is none.

claims.statement: ...Re1+ is check but not mate.
The square h2 is empty, so the king can go there.

hints: The rook can still check on e1. Is it mate?
Where could the king go?
The pawn move gave the king the h2 square.
items.explain: With the pawn on h3 the king can step to h2 after ...Re1+, so there is no mate. The one change is the luft square.

feedback_by_move.e8e1: After ...Re1+ the king steps to h2, so it is check but not mate.

items.prompt: The same position as the first, but a white knight stands on f3. Black has just moved. Anything to worry about? Show the threat or say there is none.

claims.statement: The knight on f3 covers e1.
...Re1+ Nxe1 loses the rook.

hints: The rook can reach e1. Who can take it there?
A check is only mate if the checking piece cannot be taken.
The knight on f3 covers e1.
items.explain: The knight covers e1, so ...Re1+ just loses the rook. The one change is the covered entry square.

feedback_by_move.e8e1: The knight takes the rook on e1, so the rook sacrifice only loses material.

items.prompt: Black has just moved. Black's bishop and rook both aim at the white knight on e5. Anything to worry about? Show the threat or say there is none.

claims.statement: Two black pieces attack e5.
A pawn and a rook guard e5.
Starting the exchange gains Black nothing.

hints: Count the attackers and the defenders on e5.
Who captures first, and what does the next capture cost?
Bishop takes knight, pawn takes bishop: an even swap; a rook that continues loses.
items.explain: Two attack and two guard. The bishop takes, the pawn retakes, and a rook that continues would lose to the other rook. There is no real threat.

feedback_by_move.c7e5: The pawn retakes, an even swap. A further rook capture would lose the rook to the rook on e1.

items.prompt: The same position, but a white rook stands on b1. Black has just moved. Anything to worry about? Show the threat or say there is none.

claims.statement: The bishop has no legal move.
The bishop does attack the knight.

hints: The bishop attacks the knight. Can it legally move?
Look along the b-file, from the rook.
The bishop is pinned to its king, so it cannot leave the file.
items.explain: The bishop attacks the knight, but the rook pins it to the black king, so the capture would be illegal. An attack by a pinned piece is no threat.

feedback_by_move.b6d4: That capture is illegal: the bishop is pinned to the king by the rook on b1.

items.prompt: Black's bishop has just moved to b4 and attacks your rook. Answer the threat by capturing the piece that makes it.

claims.statement: The rook on e1 is attacked and nothing guards it.
The pawn on a3 attacks the bishop.
Capturing the bishop is the engine's first choice.

hints: Which black piece makes the threat?
Can any of your pieces take it?
The pawn on a3 takes the bishop on b4.
items.explain: The bishop carries the whole threat. When the attacker can be taken for free, capturing it is the cleanest answer: the threat disappears and you are a piece up.

feedback_by_move.e1d1: The rook is safe there, but you let the bishop go for free. Capturing the attacker wins a piece.

items.prompt: Black has just played ...e5 and attacks your knight. Move the knight to a square that no black piece attacks.

claims.statement: No black piece attacks c2.
The pawn on a4 attacks b3.
The bishop on g4 attacks f3.
The bishop on g4 attacks e2.
The pawn on c6 attacks b5.
The bishop on g4 attacks f5.
The pawn on f7 and the bishop on g4 both attack e6.
The pawn on b7 guards c6.

hints: List the squares the knight can reach. Which pieces watch each one?
The bishop on g4 and the pawns on a4, c6 and f7 cover most of them.
Only c2 is free.
items.explain: Moving away is the answer most people reach for first, but the escape square must be safe too. The knight's other squares are each covered by the bishop or a pawn. Ask the threat question about your reply before you play it.

feedback_by_move.d4b3: The pawn on a4 takes the knight on b3.
feedback_by_move.d4f3: The bishop on g4 attacks f3, and you wanted a square nothing attacks.
feedback_by_move.d4e2: The bishop on g4 takes the knight on e2.
feedback_by_move.d4f5: The bishop on g4 takes the knight on f5.
feedback_by_move.d4b5: The pawn on c6 takes the knight on b5.

items.prompt: Black's rook attacks your bishop, and the knight on b1 is its only guard. Pick a quiet move that leaves no piece loose.

claims.statement: The king move is the engine's first choice at depth 16 [V]; a3 is also accepted because it leaves nothing loose (C3).
After the king move no white piece is loose.
After a3 no white piece is loose.
If the knight leaves b1, the bishop on c3 is loose.

hints: Which piece guards the bishop?
What would a knight move leave behind?
Choose a move that keeps the knight where it is.
items.explain: The knight on b1 is the bishop's only guard. Moving it removes that guard, and the rook takes the bishop. Ask what your move leaves loose before you play it.

feedback_by_move.b1d2: The knight leaves b1, so the rook takes the bishop on c3 and nothing takes back.
feedback_by_move.b1a3: The knight leaves b1, so the bishop on c3 loses its guard.
